lines.text: How deep is the deepest, darkest point on our entire planet?
The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench plunges nearly thirty-six thousand feet into the abyss.
If you took Mount Everest and placed it at the bottom, its highest snowy peak would still be over a mile underwater.
At this depth, water pressure reaches over sixteen thousand pounds per square inch.
That is equivalent to having fifty jumbo jet airplanes stacked directly on your chest.
Yet despite crushing pressure and absolute blackness, translucent ghost fish and amphipods thrive here.
We know vastly more about the craters on the Moon than the floor of our own oceans.
